narrative.overview:
The page is an open Ayacucho retablo box: a painted wooden frame whose lid folds to two plank doors, gold fillets drawing every niche, and the whole criollo carta shelved inside as 13 painted niches. Nothing floats over the page or hovers above the frame — every element lives inside the box, the way a figurine lives in a niche. The material is paint: flat field colors, zigzag painted ribbon, gold leaf used as trim and rings, wooden planks rendered as stripes.

The system reads at two registers of light. Day is lime plaster inside a red frame; night is the same box by candle and oil lamp — the whole palette swaps through five variables, never per-element restyling. Type is carved, not typeset: Grandstander carries the lettering on the box; Alegreya Sans carries what the box explains, with English always as an italic gloss.

Density is that of a real menu held at arm's length: name, gloss, price on one line each, divided by dashed pencil rules, prices ringed in gold. The page adds no imagery — the box, the ribbon, the doors, the medallion carry the surface.
keyCharacteristics: One painted box; sections are niches, never floating cards
Gold appears as fillet, ring and ribbon — never as a field above tint scale
Two light registers (day plaster / candlelit night) swapped by variables
Prices are the only pills; every price is a gold-ringed red pill
One authored motion moment (the two-beat door reveal); everything else yields
Bilingual by contrast: Spanish leads, English whispers in italic

rules.name: The Painted Register Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two color registers, day and night, and they swap as a set through the palette variables. No element may be restyled for night on its own.

rules.name: The Gold Is Trim Rule
rules.body: Gold renders as fillet, 2–4px ring, ribbon stripe or medallion. A gold field larger than a chip is forbidden; lit gold belongs to state, not decoration.

rules.name: The Italic Gloss Rule
rules.body: English is always Alegreya Sans italic in gloss ink; it is never display, never uppercase, never the same tone as its Spanish name.

rules.name: The Carved At Size Rule
rules.body: Grandstander is uppercase and tracked only at label and headline sizes; dish titles run mixed case untracked, so the display face never becomes a texture.

rules.name: The Painted Box Rule
rules.body: Nested frames — niche inside corridor inside box — are the depth system. Flattening any level breaks the retablo and is a defect, not a simplification.

rules.name: The Neutral Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every drop shadow is black-alpha, offset and blurred. A chromatic glow, a zero-offset halo, or a hard offset shadow is refused by the world.

rules.name: The Ribbon Rule
rules.body: Painted stripes exist only as ribbon: the cinta, the shelf rules, the plank surface of the doors. Stripes used as a background fill for content areas are a violation of the material.

dos: Do keep every price a retablo-red pill with a 2px gold ring and tabular numerals.
Do write English as Alegreya italic in gloss ink, following its Spanish name.
Do keep the nested frames intact (niche in corridor in box) and the 0.5rem dashed dish rhythm.
Do swap day/night only through the palette register, and honor prefers-reduced-motion by stilling the doors, the pulse and smooth scrolling.
Do name each section's notebook origin with a green ticket.
donts: Don't add photography, illustration or texture images; the material is CSS paint only.
Don't add kickers or eyebrow labels above headings, gradient text, or glyph icons.
Don't use colored glows, zero-offset halos or hard offset shadows; shadows are neutral, offset and blurred.
Don't give gold a field larger than a chip, or let lit gold escape state duty.
Don't uppercase or track dish names; carving is for the box's labels, not the food's names.
